conflicts.about: Whether the ruling's real-constraint override covers accessibility and no-JavaScript use, wherever Design Release 2.1's markup or behaviour falls short of a GOV.UK accessibility pattern the real service follows.

positions.says: Every page works fully without JavaScript, and CSS and JavaScript may only enhance a page that already works.

Only a DR1 judgement or a real constraint (persistence, validation, auth, cross-service) overrides the prototype.
The ruling does not say whether a constrained service keeps today's behaviour or matches the prototype as closely as it can.
The origin page keeps its title in an error state, with no 'Error: ' prefix.

conflicts.outcome: The real-constraint override covers accessibility and no-JavaScript use, and reaches only as far as that duty: every page follows Design Release 2.1 except where it falls short of it. The 9 October afternoon ruling, which outranks every other source, makes every page work fully without JavaScript and replaces this conflict's earlier origin, transit, transporter and CPH clauses. Start and origin: keep the 'Error: ' title prefix on the type question and the origin page, a real 'Country of origin' label on an accessible-autocomplete over a native select that works without JavaScript, and the region code input linked to its hint and error with the error style; within that build the hint and placeholder follow Design Release 2.1, while opening on focus, matching, the arrow and the announcements follow the component as the real frontend configures it (c-009). Port of entry and transit countries: keep today's native selects, the Add country button and the Remove buttons that submit the form, and today's announcements; adding a country the moment it is picked, removing one without a page load and the custom announcement wording are settled by the 13 November design ruling; keep the 'Error: ' title prefix and the visually hidden country name on each Remove. Transporters: the list's in-page filter is blocked with transporter management, and the commercial form's fields hidden behind the address search wait on the address lookup; without JavaScript the commercial form shows its fields from the start. Upload documents: keep the 'Error: ' title prefix, the error summary at the top of the main content, the attachment error after its hint, Remove buttons naming their document and link text saying it opens in a new tab; everything else follows Design Release 2.1. CPH number: the page works as today with the server's checks, and the interaction designer's 9 November ruling settles that no type behaviour is added on top. Viewed notification: the title is '<reference> - Import notification service - GOV.UK' in every state, and the journey review keeps 'Review your notification - Import notification service - GOV.UK'. Success banners (the notification list's, the deletion message and the templates pages'): no auto-dismiss; a banner stays until the trader leaves or reloads the page, and everything else about it follows Design Release 2.1.

conflicts.outcome: The prototype wins on the question itself: a start from the all-types dashboard asks 'What are you importing?' with DR2.1's title, caption, Back link, radios and Continue button before any draft exists, which the INS front door now does. Cross-service and persistence constraints override the prototype's routing, where every type continues to the live-animals origin page and a plants draft takes a GBN-AG reference: Live animals continues to the animals frontend's live-animals start, which creates the GBN-AG draft and lands on origin, and origin's Back link returns to the type question. Germinal products, offered second under the 9 October ruling, continues to the start of the germinal products set, the live-animals set's sibling in the animals frontend, which creates its own GBN-AG draft and lands on that set's origin page; a reference prefix of its own is a data shape the prototype does not decide, so the animals service's own format stands. Plants for planting, Potatoes (seed and ware) and Wood products continue to the start of the high-risk plants journey in trade-imports-plants-frontend, which creates a plants draft in that service's own reference format and lands on plants' own first page. Design Release 2.1's icon-only search button, its selection-count announcements, its 'Commodity search results' label and its Escape-empties-the-field behaviour go out of scope as that ticket's to decide (req-2229, req-2230, req-2231). Ruling 2026-10-09's reason for keeping inc-014 (claim 117) stays withdrawn, and the 9 October afternoon design wait is replaced by the 10 November handover; ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm-p1-059 and -p1-060 are not overruled, because they also record that today's server-side search works without JavaScript, which req-1918 keeps. Other live mammals holds both 'Other mammalia' and 'Other Mammalia', each 'Other mammal'.

A real constraint the prototype cannot express, such as cross-service behaviour, overrides the prototype default.

conflicts.outcome: Correct DR2.1's species data rather than copy it: the horse species reads 'Equus caballus' and the mule 'Eq caballus*asinus', and Other live mammals holds a single 'Other Mammalia' (Other mammal) entry. The species display text is what the backend sends downstream as the GBN-AG scientificName, with no species code beside it, so a misspelt Latin name would reach the receiving service as a wrong scientific name, and two entries that differ only in a capital letter would reach it as the same species. The prototype's own id (horse-equus-caballus) already spells the name correctly. Every other species name, common name and code is exactly as DR2.1 gives it. The misspelling has since reached the real catalogue (repo-tests-p1-130), which the catalogue's owner, MDM, corrects: the correction is a content report, not a code change (req-101).

The frontend has since built the forward half (req-087, req-117, req-118) and the commodity page's trail-following back link (req-089); only Commodity details' back link is still the overview's (req-108). Nothing is overruled: repo-frontend-p9-054's trail is what returns the trader to the origin page in the journey and to the overview when the overview sent them, and repo-frontend-p10-008 records the behaviour req-108's delta cites.

Results show the lookup's formatted address line. What else the search needs is settled when the area is re-distilled after the lookup lands.

Postcode stays free text, as in every source; whether phone gains a format check is c-256.

conflicts.about: Error-state accessibility the prototype leaves out: no 'Error:' title prefix, and error summary links to fields that stay hidden on the search layout.

The address book manages transporters: a transporter is a record held per organisation in trade-imports-address-book, in a transporters collection of its own with its own document, controller, repository and route, reusing the service's organisation scoping, soft-delete, locking and Standard Address Block validation, holding no role and storing a private-or-commercial type instead (req-2260 to req-2263). Every row that changes how transporters are listed, searched or added therefore goes ahead: the list's heading, search, columns, 'Not applicable' cell and 'View details' link, the type page's wording, both add forms and what follows a save, the private transporter's country list, the address book's transporter rows and its Transporter tab, and the list's paging (req-2268). Much of it has since landed on the animals frontend and in the address book, so this re-distil records most of those rows as already existing rather than as changes; where the address book's own add pages read differently from the design the difference is its own row (req-2265 to req-2267). What goes ahead over today's step is unchanged: its place in the journey (req-405), its amend and template-review buttons (req-407, req-408), the germinal set's own transporter step (req-1820) and the step's mandatory-to-proceed check (req-402, c-346). Approved transporters are parked, so the eight records the service ships stay exactly as they are and which approved-transporter list the commercial ones come from stays open (req-397, req-398, req-2172, c-057). The register page removal is already done on main (EUDPA-739, inc-044), which the traces predate (req-472).

Nothing is overruled. ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm-p2-031, -p2-033 and -p2-034 blocked transporter management pending further requirements and -p2-050 noted that nobody was named to produce them; those requirements have now been given, so the claims are satisfied rather than withdrawn, and -p2-035's instruction to re-distil the area once it was decided is what this run carries out.

On either save button the trader sees an error for each answer that is missing or not valid.
DR1 parity built the origin page saving a partly answered page with no country of origin, instead of refusing to save.
inc-082 brought origin into line with the pages that save an empty answer.
Country of origin stays mandatory for completeness: the hub shows the origin task unfinished without it and the review page stops a submission without it.
The origin page does not validate the country of origin, and no message for a missing or invalid country is defined.
An empty country of origin is not an error: only the region code error is raised.
Returning to the origin page after a save with no country shows the country still empty.
A notification saved with no country of origin keeps it empty on return.
A country of origin must now be chosen before the page can be saved, and leaving it blank shows 'Select a country of origin'.
Submitting the origin page with no country saved without any error.

conflicts.outcome: The V4 data page outranks DR1's parity judgement, the prototype and the real frontend on whether a field is mandatory, and its most recent change (2 November 2026, at the business's request) makes Country of origin mandatory to proceed. In the live-animals and germinal products sets the origin page is saved only with a country, on Save and continue and on Save and return to overview alike, which is also what the 26 October ruling requires of the two buttons (req-032); the animals frontend already refuses the blank country, and the Save and return half arrives with the page's return controls (req-051). Cancel and return to overview still leaves the page without saving, and the field stays mandatory for completeness too, so document-dr1-parity-backlog-p4-035 is kept: a notification whose origin page was never saved still shows the origin task 'To do' and is still stopped at the check page. High-risk plants already refuses a blank country with its own message, so nothing changes there. The claims from the real services are not overruled: they are the evidence of what the change replaced. Where a countryless save would have landed no longer arises, so that requirement is recorded as set aside (req-033) and c-004's own overruled claims stay as they are.

conflicts.about: What the animals origin page says when no country of origin is given.

positions.says: Country of origin is mandatory to proceed, but the page gives no message for a missing one.
No message for a missing or invalid country is defined, though the view has a slot to show one.
A blank country is refused with 'Select a country of origin', a country outside the list with 'Select a country from the list'.
The end-to-end suite proves 'Select a country of origin' in the summary and against the field.
Plants refuses a blank or unlisted country with 'Select the country where the consignment originates from'.

conflicts.outcome: The V4 data page outranks every other source on whether the field is mandatory, and it is silent on the wording, as Design Release 2.1 is: nothing above the real services names a message, so each frontend's own wording stands. The animals origin page, in the live-animals and germinal products sets, shows 'Select a country of origin' for a missing country and keeps 'Select a country from the list' for one outside the list (req-2123), and the high-risk plants origin page keeps its own 'Select the country where the consignment originates from' (req-1913). Nothing is overruled here: prototype-dr2-1-source-p2-059 is already set aside by c-319.

conflicts.about: Whether the origin page's Save and return to overview makes the same checks as Save and continue.

positions.says: Save and return to overview makes exactly the same checks as Save and continue, on every page that has both buttons, with no page an exception.
Today Save and return to overview skips the checks Save and continue makes, the origin page among them.
The earlier ruling on this behaviour is not to be assumed right, because the BA is the one raising it.
Pages with an exit to the overview save without their required checks, in plants as well, and only a malformed answer is refused.
The animals origin page has no Save and return to overview at all today.
Plants' Save and return to overview already makes the same checks as Save and continue and saves nothing when they fail.
Saving the origin page with the return-to-overview action skips validation and saves the draft.

conflicts.outcome: The 26 October ruling is the most authoritative source on Save and return and withdraws the earlier soft save: on the origin page, in the live-animals and germinal products sets and in high-risk plants, Save and return to overview makes exactly the checks Save and continue makes, and a failure keeps the trader on the page with an error for each answer that is missing or not valid and what they entered still shown (req-2124). Plants already behaves this way; in animals the button is not on the page at all, so the behaviour arrives with the return controls, which the 10 November ruling blocks on the EUDPA-774 save and continue work. The checks are the page's own, so a blank answer to the region of origin code requirement is still accepted: the V4 data page makes that field mandatory to submit rather than to proceed (req-047). The germinal products set takes the rule because each germinal page is a copy of its live-animals twin, which settles the set scope the ruling leaves open. The whole-journey soft save (c-211) and its plants counterpart (c-313) are replaced where those conflicts are kept, and ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm-p3-027 is not overruled here because it still has plants take the change in the same increment.

conflicts.about: Whether the region of origin code is chosen from a reference list or typed.

positions.says: Region of origin code's values come from MDM.
Region of origin code is a string of at most five characters, shown and stored with an ISO country prefix taken from the country of origin.
The region of origin code is typed into a five-character box after the country prefix.
The trader types the part after the fixed country prefix, and no region list is read.

conflicts.outcome: The V4 data page's source cell reads two ways and nothing ranks them: either the field's MDM source is only the country prefix it is built from, or the regions themselves come from a list the trader picks from. The two build different things, so it goes to the owner with a default that changes nothing.
conflicts.question: Does the region of origin code come from a list of regions served for the chosen country, or stay a code the trader types?
conflicts.default: It stays a code the trader types into the five-character box after the country prefix, in both animals sets: the V4 page names no region list, no reference-data endpoint serves one, and Design Release 2.1 and the real page both have a typed box. No region list is built and no reference-data work is raised.

conflicts.about: Whether 'Save and return to overview' on the commodity pages skips the page's checks: Design Release 2.1 and the 9 October afternoon ruling make it a soft save, the 26 October ruling makes it run the same checks as 'Save and continue'.

positions.says: Saving the commodity page with the return-to-overview action skips validation, saves any valid selection and goes to the overview.
The soft save overwrites the saved species with the empty submitted list, wiping an earlier selection.
'Save and return to overview' goes to the overview without validating, even with no commodity selected.
With nothing selected the button posts the empty selection and redirects to the overview with no error.
After returning with nothing selected, the overview shows 'What are you importing?' as To do.
req-088, Save and return to overview without checks, is not catalogue or search work and goes ahead in inc-011.
Save and return to overview makes exactly the same checks as Save and continue.
The same-checks rule applies on every page that has both buttons, in live animals and in high-risk plants.
No page is an exception to the same-checks rule.
Each germinal page is a copy of its live-animals feature folder plus the prototype's germinal differences.
Both save buttons make the same checks.
Clearing a saved commodity selection and pressing Save and return to overview is refused with Select a commodity, holds the trader on the page and leaves the selection saved before intact.
Save and return to overview on the plants commodity type page makes the same checks as Save and continue, refusing a blank or unoffered answer at 400 and saving nothing.

conflicts.outcome: The 26 October ruling, the highest-ranked source, wins: on the commodity page, on Commodity details and on the plants commodity type page 'Save and return to overview' makes exactly the same checks as 'Save and continue', refusing a missing or invalid answer with its own error, keeping the trader on the page with what they entered, and saving and returning to the overview once the page is valid (req-088, req-120, req-2136). All three now behave that way (repo-tests-p1-125, repo-plantsfrontend-p3-047-m1, ruling-sam-2026-11-10b-p1-012). This withdraws the soft save the 9 October afternoon ruling carried for the commodity page; ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm-p2-007 is not overruled, because it also moves req-085 and req-102 out of the MDM-blocked search work, which still stands. The germinal set's copies of these two pages take the same checks, because each germinal page is a copy of its live-animals twin. trace-prototype-dr2-1-p3-048 is not overruled: the overview still shows 'What are you importing?' as To do while nothing is chosen, which a trader now reaches by cancelling rather than by saving and returning.

conflicts.about: Which commodities the Number of packages question is asked for: Design Release 2.1's packaging-fields list, or the data fields page's package-count list of 54 commodities.

positions.says: Only cattle, horse, pig, sheep, goat, cat, dog, ferret and other live mammals have packaging fields.
Chicken, turkey, duck, goose, guinea fowl, rabbit, camel, ostrich, parrot, reptile, bees and ornamental fish show only Number of animals.
For poultry the species block asks only for Number of animals.
For chickens the commodity details page shows no number of packages field.
Number of packages is shown only where a package count applies to the selected commodity.
The package count applies to 54 named commodities, poultry, game birds, rabbits, reptiles, psittaciformes, rodents, insects, bees and the semen, embryo and ova lines among them.
The number of packages field is shown only for the commodity codes the frontend's own applicability rules say packages apply to.
The prototype decides look and feel only: content, wording, layout, components, question order, and which questions are asked of which goods.
V4 is the source of truth for data: no row may rest on the prototype's app/data files for which commodities a rule covers.

conflicts.outcome: The data fields page wins on which commodities the rule covers, and ruling 11 November makes that a standing rule: the specification ranks above the prototype for which commodity codes each conditional rule applies to, while the prototype's commodity entries are demo fixture data. So the question is asked wherever the specification's package-count list names the chosen species' commodity, poultry, game birds, rabbits, reptiles, psittaciformes, rodents, insects, bees and the semen, embryo and ova lines included, and is withheld elsewhere (req-112). Ruling 2026-10-09's claim that the prototype decides which questions are asked of which goods is not overruled: it ranks the prototype above what the real services do today, not above the data specification, and the prototype still gives the field its label and hint. prototype-dr2-1-source-p3-026 is not overruled either, because it carries that label and hint; only its list of packaging commodities is set aside, which p3-027 states on its own. Which commodity code each list entry maps to in the catalogue is MDM's content to serve.

conflicts.about: What 'numeric - max 10' limits on the live-animal Number of packages: the number of digits, or the number of packages.

positions.says: Number of packages is a numeric value of at most 10 digits.
The page does not say whether 'max 10' is a digit count or a maximum value, and its own examples for the field are 1, 25 and 5000.
Example numbers of packages are 1, 25 and 5000.
The number of packages is capped at 2,147,483,647, the largest whole number the service that stores it holds.

conflicts.outcome: Nothing ranks the two readings: the same table writes 'max 9,223,372,036,854,775,807' as a value for the number of animals and the germinal quantity row's 'max 1,000' was read as a value too, while this row's own examples of 25 and 5000 can only be digit counts. It goes to the owner with the digit reading as the default, which the service already satisfies: its cap of 2,147,483,647 is the largest ten-digit whole number it can store.
conflicts.question: Does the live-animal Number of packages allow up to 10 digits, or at most 10 packages, given that the same table's germinal quantity row reads 'max 1,000' as a maximum value while this row's own examples are 25 and 5000?
conflicts.default: The digit reading is kept, as the only reading the row's own examples allow: the field is capped at the largest whole number the notification stores, 2,147,483,647, which is ten digits, with an error naming that figure on that species' number of packages field. No cap of 10 packages is built, because it would refuse an example the specification itself gives.

conflicts.about: The agreed maximum number of species a trader may choose under one commodity.

positions.says: The trader may select one or more species up to the agreed maximum.
The page does not give the number behind the agreed maximum, so the limit to enforce is unknown.
Nothing on either commodity page limits how many commodity lines a notification may hold.
No test runs a search that returns many results, so any limit on a large selection is not shown.

conflicts.outcome: The specification states that a maximum exists but not what it is, and no ruling gives a number, so it goes to the owner with no cap as the default.
conflicts.question: What is the agreed maximum number of species a trader may choose under one commodity?
conflicts.default: No maximum is enforced, as today, so a trader may choose every species a commodity offers; a cap and its error are built only once the number is given.

conflicts.about: Whether 'Applies at: Commodity Level' puts the number of animals and the number of packages once per commodity, covering all its species, or once per commodity line.

positions.says: Number of animals (quantity) applies at Commodity Level.
Number of packages applies at Commodity Level.
Species selection is a multi-select that also applies at Commodity Level, so one commodity may carry several species.
Number of animals is asked per species, in a field named for that species.
Saving a chosen set of species writes one commodity line for each, holding its commodity code, Latin name and common name, with the quantities hanging off the line.

conflicts.outcome: The two readings build different pages, one field per commodity or one per species, and nothing ranks them: the specification gives the level but never says what a commodity line holds. It goes to the owner with the per-species reading as the default.
conflicts.question: Does one number of animals and one number of packages cover every species chosen under a commodity, or does each chosen species have its own pair, as the real service's commodity line and Design Release 2.1 both have it?
conflicts.default: Each chosen species keeps its own number of animals and number of packages, as today and as Design Release 2.1 shows, because the real service's commodity line is one commodity plus one species and each line's species travels downstream on its own; the germinal set's per-species packages and total gross weight stay per species for the same reason.

conflicts.about: Which commodity and species names the live-animals catalogue shows: Design Release 2.1's list, the data fields page's examples, or whatever MDM serves.

positions.says: Cattle, code 0102, carries the 11 cattle species of the 0102 list.
The cattle species and their common names run from Bibos spp. (Gaur) to Syncerus spp. (African buffalo), with Bos taurus named Domestic cattle and Bison bison named Bison bison.
Species selection's values come from MDM.
An example commodity selection is 'Cattle, 0102, Bos taurus', so the page names code 0102 Cattle.
Example species selections are Bison bison (Bison), Bos spp. (Cattle species), Bos taurus (Cattle) and Bubalus bubalis (Water buffalo).
Where a list's content differs from Design Release 2.1, that is MDM's content to change, never a reason to block a row or to edit a list in code.
A reference list is MDM's content, reaching the service through trade-imports-reference-data, never a reason to block a row and never edited in code.

conflicts.outcome: The rulings and the data fields page agree that the catalogue's content is MDM's: the commodity and species names the page shows are whatever MDM serves through reference-data (req-2130), so no name is edited in code to match Design Release 2.1 or the page's examples. The catalogue rows (req-094 to req-101) are out of scope as MDM content rather than blocked work, and each commodity's and species' name, the three the page's examples spell differently (Bison bison, Bos spp. and Bos taurus) included, is MDM's to serve. Nothing is overruled: Design Release 2.1's list still records what the design shows and the examples still record the specification's naming, and the content report weighs both against MDM's. The page's own example names code 0102 Cattle, which the catalogue now does too (req-095).

conflicts.about: Whether numbers typed on Commodity details but not yet saved survive a Remove.

positions.says: Numbers typed into a surviving commodity's fields but not yet saved are kept on the page after another commodity is removed.
The remove form does not carry unsaved typed counts, so the remaining species' inputs come back empty.
What a trader typed is never dropped.

conflicts.outcome: The 26 October ruling wins, and the frontend now keeps what the trader has typed: the numbers are still in their fields when Commodity details comes back, and a surviving line the post names no count for shows its stored value (req-1759). The trace of the empty inputs is not overruled, because it records the earlier behaviour that requirement's delta cites.

conflicts.about: The typed form the exit date accepts and the example its hint shows: DD/MM/YYYY with 27/03/2026, or one or two digits for day and month with 'For example, 27/3/2026'.

positions.says: The exit date must be a valid date entered in DD/MM/YYYY format.
The example value given for the exit date is 27/03/2026.
Where V4 specifies a field's format, V4 decides it and the prototype decides how the field reads.
An exit date is accepted in day/month/year form with a four-digit year and one or two digits for day and month.
The exit date hint is 'For example, 27/3/2026'.
The MOJ date picker fills the field as day/month/year without leading zeros, under the hint 'For example, 27/3/2026'.

conflicts.outcome: Unsettled. The 11 November ruling puts the format with V4 and how the field reads with the prototype, which splits the hint from the accepted form and leaves the field refusing the very text its own picker writes: the accepted MOJ date picker fills it without leading zeros, so a strict two-digit rule cannot be met by the component the page is built from. Neither reading of 'DD/MM/YYYY', a digit count or the day-month-year order, is ranked above the other.
conflicts.question: Must the exit date be typed with a two-digit day and month, with the hint example 27/03/2026, or is a single-digit day or month still accepted with the hint example 27/3/2026?
conflicts.default: The field keeps the hint 'For example, 27/3/2026' and accepts a day or month with or without a leading zero, because the accepted date picker fills it that way; V4's DD/MM/YYYY is read as naming the day, month and year order rather than a stricter digit count. If the strict reading is chosen instead, the hint example becomes 27/03/2026 and the picker is configured to write leading zeros, so the field never refuses its own output.

conflicts.about: Whether the germinal products set captures an exit date, which the copy rule would carry across from live animals while the only reasons the set offers never ask for one.

positions.says: The germinal reason page offers only Internal market and Transit, neither of which asks for an exit date.
Each germinal page is a copy of its live-animals feature folder plus the prototype's germinal differences, which carries the live-animals exit date page across.

The germinal section names only the county parish holding number and the permanent address as not required for germinal products, and does not say which other live-animal fields the germinal journey drops or keeps.

conflicts.outcome: Unsettled. The copy rule carries every live-animals page into the germinal set, and the data page's germinal section says nothing about which other live-animal fields the set drops, while Design Release 2.1's germinal journey offers only two reasons and never reaches the one reason that asks for an exit date. The two readings build different germinal journeys, and nothing ranks them.
conflicts.question: Does the germinal products set ask for an exit date, or does it keep only Internal market and Transit so no exit date is ever captured there?
conflicts.default: The germinal products set offers only Internal market and Transit, asks for no exit date and builds nothing for one; the live-animals set keeps its own exit date question.

conflicts.about: Whether 'Save and return to overview' on the main import reason and additional details pages skips the checks that 'Save and continue' makes.

positions.says: Save and return to overview makes exactly the same checks as Save and continue.
No page is an exception to the same-checks rule.
Save and return to overview saves without any validation and goes to the notification hub.
On a hub or review save an invalid or missing follow-up is saved as empty.
On a hub or review save with no reason selected, nothing on the page is changed.
Save and return to overview on additional details saves each answer only if it is one of the offered options and goes to the hub without validating.
When amending, Save and return goes to the review page.

conflicts.outcome: The 26 October ruling outranks every other source: on both pages 'Save and return to overview' runs exactly the checks 'Save and continue' runs, keeps the trader on the page with an error for each missing or invalid answer, and shows the overview only when every answer passes. The re-extracted animals frontend already behaves that way on both pages (repo-frontend-p8-117, repo-frontend-p8-137). The ruling withdraws the earlier soft-save decision recorded in c-211 and its plants counterpart c-313, so the prototype's save-without-validation claims are overruled. Three claims are left out: prototype-dr2-1-source-p4-076 and prototype-dr2-1-source-p4-077 still say where the button goes when amending and that editing a template saves the template and returns to its review, and prototype-dr2-1-source-p4-078 still backs the purge of other reasons' answers (req-156) even though its saving a missing follow-up as empty is set aside.

conflicts.about: Whether a species whose commodity requires no specific identifier type is asked for free-text identifiers, or asked nothing at all.

positions.says: The identification details field is shown when the given commodity has no specific identifier type, and captures free-text identification details.
The animal description field is shown on the same condition and captures a free-text animal description.
Where the commodity has no specific identifier type the two free-text fields stand in for one, so every commodity has some way of identifying its animals.
The page does not list which commodities have no specific identifier type, so the set can only be read as everything absent from the passport, tattoo, ear tag and horse name lists.
A species' identifier fields come from its commodity's entry in the identifiers list, and where there is no entry there are none.
For poultry there is no identification page at all: commodity details goes straight to additional details.
No field labelled 'Identification details' or 'Animal description' appears for any commodity walked.

conflicts.outcome: The policy page ranks above the prototype, its traces and the real frontend, and sources.json makes it the specification of which data a notification captures, outranking the prototype on data even where a prototype claim says otherwise. The two free-text identifiers are built (req-2149, req-2150, req-2151), so every selected species has a panel (req-210, req-221), and the frontend has since made the change (repo-frontend-p10-091, repo-frontend-p10-146). Which commodities fall back is read as everything absent from the policy page's four identifier lists (confluence-6497338582-p4-061); in today's catalogue that is Atlantic salmon and the ostrich the tests repo drives. prototype-dr2-1-source-p5-013 is not overruled: its first half, that a species' identifier fields come from its commodity's own list, still stands and backs req-2146, and only its 'otherwise there are none' half is set aside. prototype-dr2-1-specs-p4-017 keeps backing the half that still stands, that a species which needs identifying continues to the page. trace-e2e-p6-017 describes the page the traces were captured against, which req-221 changed.

conflicts.about: Whether a tattoo identifier is asked for on cattle (0102) and pigs (0103), as V4's tattoo commodity list says, or only on cats, dogs and ferrets, as its list title's count of two, DR2.1 and today's service suggest.

positions.says: The commodities that require a tattoo identifier are 01061900 cats, dogs and ferrets, 0103 pigs and 0102 bovine.
The tattoo list's title says two commodities while five entries are listed, and the page does not say which figure is right.
The page names code 0102 'Cattle' in the passport and ear tag lists but 'Bovine' in the tattoo list.
Commodity code 0102 asks for two identifiers only, ear tag and passport.
Commodity code 0103 asks for one identifier, an ear tag.
A tattoo asked for on every cow is a defect of the real frontend's tattoo allowlist, and inc-110 corrects the commodity identifier sets.
Conflict c-334 is settled by following the policy page's tattoo list.
The five entries listed in the tattoo expand win over the title's count of two.
The deliberate removal of the tattoo from cattle under DR1 parity is reversed, by this ruling rather than silently.
A cattle line asks for an ear tag, then a passport, then a tattoo.

conflicts.outcome: The 11 November ruling ranks first and settles it: the policy page's list is followed, so a tattoo is asked for on cattle (0102) and on pigs (0103) as well as on cats, dogs and ferrets (req-2154, req-2155), the entries listed beat the list title's count of two, and naming code 0102 'Bovine' in this list and 'Cattle' in the others is a label difference rather than a difference of scope. DR1's note that a tattoo on a cow is a defect, and the deliberate DR1 parity commit behind it, are set aside: the ruling is the reversal. prototype-dr2-1-source-p5-015 and prototype-dr2-1-source-p5-017 are not overruled, because the ear tag and passport they give cattle and the ear tag they give pigs still stand (req-216, req-219); only their 'and no other identifier' half is set aside. The frontend has since made the change (repo-frontend-p10-093, repo-frontend-p10-097).

conflicts.about: Whether the notification still captures a microchip identifier, which V4's six animal identifier fields leave out.

positions.says: Six animal identifier fields are specified, at least one of which must be given, and none of them is a microchip.
The six animal identifier fields apply to the live animals journey only.
The page de-scopes an identifier type explicitly when it means to: the wing ring was de-scoped on 29 May 2026.
Commodity code 01061900 asks for a microchip, a passport and a tattoo.
Commodity code 0101 asks for a microchip, a passport and a horse name.
The identifier types the page can ask for are microchip, passport, tattoo, ear tag, horse name, identification details and description.

conflicts.outcome: The default keeps the microchip field, on cat, dog, ferret and horse panels, as DR2.1 shows it and the service asks for it today (req-2153, req-222, req-223). V4 outranks the prototype on which data a notification captures, but it never says the microchip is out of scope, and it de-scopes a field explicitly when it means to, as it did for the wing ring; silence will not carry a user-visible field away.
conflicts.question: Does a notification still capture a microchip identifier, given that V4's animal identifier table specifies six fields and the microchip is not one of them, while the page de-scopes only the wing ring explicitly?
conflicts.default: The microchip field stays exactly as it is today and as Design Release 2.1 shows it, first on a cat, dog, ferret or horse panel.

conflicts.about: How much identification a live-animals notification must hold before it can be submitted: an identifier for every animal, or one identified animal per species and nothing at all when one species is selected.

positions.says: A notification cannot be submitted unless at least one animal identifier is given for each animal.
Design release 1's submit gate needs only one complete animal per species, and only when more than one species is selected.
Identification details are optional when only one species is selected; with several, each species with identifier fields needs at least one entry.
Sam's acceptance of one identifier being enough holds 'for now' and assumes it is a no-change, and the ruling does not say what happens if it turns out to need a change.
The ruling does not state how many identification records a notification with several lines needs.
A commodity line counts as short of its identified animals when the records holding at least one identifier are fewer than its number of animals.

conflicts.outcome: The default follows the policy page, which is what the frontend now does: a line is short of its identified animals until every animal on it holds a record with at least one identifier (repo-frontend-p10-151, repo-frontend-p10-152), so identification is no longer optional for a single species (req-248, req-249). The 9 October ruling outranks the policy page and accepted the older gate on the footing that it was no change, but that footing has gone: the service has since moved to the per-animal bar, and the ruling expressly does not say how many records a notification needs. The germinal twin of this question went the policy page's way too (c-277), so the default now leaves the two sets on the same bar. It stays a question because only the owner can say whether the ruling was meant to fix the looser gate.
conflicts.question: Must every animal of every selected species carry at least one identifier before a live-animals notification can be submitted, as the V4 data-fields page says and as the frontend now gates, or does the looser gate the 9 October ruling accepted stand, with identification optional for a single species?
conflicts.default: The per-animal bar the frontend now applies stands: every animal of every commodity line that is identified needs a saved record holding at least one identifier, and the hub's Identification details row shows Complete on that same bar.

conflicts.about: Whether the 26 October ruling's principle that what a trader typed is never dropped reaches the identification page's own save buttons and a panel save, or only the Enter key on a panel for several animals.

positions.says: What a trader typed is never dropped, stated as a general principle and not limited to the identification page.
The recommendations Sam accepted are not quoted in the ruling, so how far the principle was meant to reach cannot be checked against his own words.
Save and continue saves the typed details only for single-animal species; what was typed into a multi-animal species' form is not saved unless its panel button was used.
A panel save validates and saves only that species' fields.
A press of one card's save button reads only that card's identifier fields, so another card's typed values are neither saved nor validated.
Save and continue reads only the cards of lines that hold one animal, so an identifier typed into a multi-animal card is neither saved nor reported back.

conflicts.outcome: The default follows the prototype, which is what the frontend now does: every save reads only the panel it owns, so a panel save checks and saves that panel alone and the page's own buttons save the single-animal panels (req-203, req-204). The earlier default rested on the service saving every panel holding a value, and that footing has gone (repo-frontend-p10-141, repo-frontend-p10-141-m1, repo-tests-p1-140-m1). It stays a question because the 26 October ruling ranks above the prototype and states the principle that what a trader typed is never dropped in general terms, while its words reach only the Enter key and the recommendation behind the principle is not quoted; answering it the other way would have each save sweep up every panel again.
conflicts.question: Does 'what a trader typed is never dropped' apply to the identification page's 'Save and continue', 'Save and return to overview' and panel save buttons, so each of them saves every panel holding a value, or only to pressing Enter in a panel for several animals?

On the consignment addresses page and the party pickers nothing new is refused: the page saves and moves on with sections still empty on either button, in the live-animals set, in the germinal-products copy and on plants' pages with both buttons, and a party picker saves with nothing chosen and no error; completeness is still enforced by the overview task status and by the review page's 'Complete consignment addresses' error, and a picker still refuses an address the organisation's book does not hold.

The port of entry is chosen through a search box with a results list labelled 'Port search results'.
Transit countries are added through a search with a results list labelled 'Country search results'.
Both searches are the service's accessible autocomplete, with the page's own polite status region and no results-list label of their own.

conflicts.outcome: The rulings rank first. Sam's 9 November answer drops the prototype's custom search-results label and 'Selected' announcement from the country search, and the 9 October afternoon ruling's toolbox rule carries the same answer to the port of entry and transit country searches, which are the same accessible autocomplete in the same service: a hand-built results-list label over the component is exactly the custom JavaScript written to copy the prototype that the ruling bars. The 9 November answer names the three origin pages, but it answers the component and not one page, so nothing is built for the labels anywhere and the searches keep the component's own announcements plus the page's status region (req-355). Neither prototype claim is overruled, because each still backs the search's placeholder and its search button (req-294, req-296, req-346); only the results-list labels are set aside.

conflicts.about: Where a port whose MDM traffic value is missing, or is not Airport, Port or Rail, sits in the port of entry list once the list is grouped by port type.

conflicts.outcome: The ruling names three groups and says MDM's traffic field already gives each port's type, but it never says what becomes of a port whose traffic is blank or holds some other value, and Sam has not confirmed the field is the flag he asked about. Sorting such a port into the seaports, leaving it out of the list, and giving it a group of its own build different lists, and nothing in the sources ranks those readings, so the question goes to the owner with a default that keeps every port MDM returns on the page (req-2259).
conflicts.question: Where should a port whose MDM traffic value is missing, or is not Airport, Port or Rail, sit in the port of entry list?
conflicts.default: Such a port is listed in its own group after the rail ports, A to Z by name, so no port MDM returns is left out of the list; airports, seaports and rail keep their order ahead of it.

conflicts.about: Where the transporter add pages live and which route a trader takes to them, now that both the animals frontend and the INS front door serve a set.

conflicts.outcome: The 6 November ruling ranks above both repos and settles it: the add pages the INS front door serves are the one route to adding a transporter, reached from the journey through the hand-off already built for addresses and from the address book's own address type question. The ruling handed this re-distil the question of what becomes of the animals frontend's three transporter add-page folders, and the rest of the ruling answers it: keeping them would be the second pattern point 2 refuses, so they go, with their routes, fit specs and copy keys, and the journey's 'Add a transporter' hands off instead (req-2264). Both of the animals frontend's details pages are signed off, so the change goes through the signed-off check. Design Release 2.1's content for those pages is unaffected: it is built on the pages that remain, and the increment that moves the route carries over anything the address book's pages do not yet show, such as the validation messages and length limits repo-tests-p15-054 and repo-tests-p15-055 record as unproven there. The germinal set therefore copies the transporter list only, not the add pages (req-1820).

conflicts.about: Whether the transporter list pages, now that transporters are records the address book holds per organisation.

positions.says: Pagination is kept and is wanted, and its earlier removal was an error: every address book list and every address picker pages.

conflicts.outcome: The 25 November ruling ranks first and is unqualified: pagination is kept everywhere, every address book list and every address picker pages, and no requirement says a list of an organisation's records is served or shown unpaginated. Transporters are now records the address book holds per organisation (req-2260), so the transporter list is such a picker and it pages, at eight, the one figure the INS address book list already uses and every other picker in both journeys takes. The 23 November ruling is not a position against this: it refuses the transporter list as a precedent for the pickers' page size precisely because the list has no paging yet, and names the still-to-do ticket that splits it into pages of eight, which is the same figure. The 'Selected address' restatement that comes back with the paging comes back here too, naming the chosen transporter, because the chosen row can be on another page (req-2268). The list's one-table rendering is set aside; it is cited as the delta in req-2268's note rather than as a claim.

A list that arrives with a search term already in its box is narrowed in the browser as soon as the page loads.
With JavaScript running, typing in the search box narrows the listed transporters without loading a new page.

conflicts.outcome: The 9 October afternoon ruling says in terms that this list's in-page filter waits for design's answer to question 5 and takes it when the area is re-distilled, and design answered on 13 November: searching is built without live filtering, the trader types a term and presses Search or Enter, and rows that filter as the trader types are not built. Design's ruling ranks above the animals frontend, so the browser filter the service now has is set aside and the list's search is the server-side one behind the button and Enter, which already exists (req-389). The bolding of matching letters goes with the filter that drew it, being part of the as-you-type behaviour design did not keep; the shown-count sentence stays and is rendered with the page the server returns (req-2269). The prototype's client-side module is not overruled, because it is also the evidence for the search box and its joined button, which stand (req-388).

conflicts.about: Which Northern Ireland country code a commercial transporter is stored with: the code the 6 November ruling names, or the one the address book already uses.

positions.says: The country code persisted for a commercial transporter is XI, displayed as 'Northern Ireland', with both held as constants in the service.
The question put was whether MDM is used for a Northern Ireland country lookup or a created commercial transporter is simply forced to a Northern Ireland country code.
A commercial transporter's fixed country is stored as the code GB-NIR and shown as the words 'Northern Ireland' by both the address book and the journey.
A transporter created through the address book API is stored with the country code GB-NIR when it is commercial and GB when it is private.

conflicts.outcome: The 6 November ruling can be read two ways and nothing ranks them. Read as a value, it names XI and justifies it against the estate's own schemas, so the address book's constant changes and the records already stored with GB-NIR are rewritten. Read as a decision between an MDM lookup and a forced code, which is how the question was put to the owner, it settles only that the code is forced, and which code the service holds is how the shape is held in code, the real service's own call, which it has already made as GB-NIR. The two readings build different things in two services, and no trader sees either code, both being shown as the words 'Northern Ireland'.
conflicts.question: Is a commercial transporter's country stored as the literal code XI, or as the Northern Ireland country code the address book already uses?
conflicts.default: Keep what is built: the address book stores the fixed country as GB-NIR, its private counterpart as GB, and both the address book and the journey show it as 'Northern Ireland' (req-2275). Nothing is rewritten. The rule that a commercial transporter must be in Northern Ireland stays enforceable from the stored value alone either way, because the code is distinct from the United Kingdom's (req-2276).

Read one way the form is the only guard, which leaves a transporter written straight through the address book's API free of the rule; read the other the address book refuses it too, which is a second check to build and a second place to keep the constant. The two readings build different things in different repos, and nothing ranks them.
conflicts.question: Does the address book refuse a commercial transporter whose country is not Northern Ireland, or is the add form the only place the rule is enforced?
conflicts.default: Both: the add form fixes the country, posts it in a hidden field and refuses a tampered, empty or absent value (req-455), and the address book refuses a commercial transporter whose country is not Northern Ireland on write, because it is the system of record and its API can be called directly (req-2277).

conflicts.question: In journey mode, does the address book's 'Add a commercial transporter' page show the notification's status strip, as Design Release 2.1 has it, or does journey mode carry no notification status at all?
conflicts.default: Follow Design Release 2.1 where the hand-off can carry it: 'Add a commercial transporter' shows the 'Draft' tag and the notification reference above its heading and neither 'Choose a transporter type' nor 'Add a private transporter' shows one (req-2278). Where journey mode cannot carry the notification's status, none of the three pages shows one, the pages are otherwise unchanged, and the difference from the design is recorded for design rather than worked around.

Consignment parties' and 'Roles and addresses' and change with req-585. prototype-dr2-1-source-p8-002 rests on the 'Consignment parties' caption alone and is wholly set aside, so it is listed as overruled. Two claims are only partly set aside and so are not overruled: prototype-dr2-1-source-p8-051 and prototype-dr2-1-specs-p3-004 each carry that caption alongside the picker's heading and intro and the page's intro paragraph, and only their caption half goes, so req-586 and req-557 keep citing them. Both give the trader the same eight rows, so no requirement about what a user sees turns on it, but the two differ in what the frontend sends and in how a book of thousands behaves.
conflicts.question: Should each party picker ask the address book's list API for its page of eight, or keep reading the role-filtered list whole and cutting the page in the frontend?
conflicts.default: Each picker keeps reading the role-filtered list the address book returns and cuts its page of eight in the frontend, as both frontends do today, and the address book's page and pageSize parameters stay for its other callers. The address book's own list, and the INS address book list page, keep paging through the API.

Its ground holds with full force here: the page writes the same address-book record the view and edit pages show County on, so an add form without County would lose the field on a round trip, which is a real persistence constraint the prototype cannot express under ruling:sam-2026-10-07 claim 10. Ruling:ian-2026-11-11 ranks higher but pulls both ways and names no field: its claim 15 gives the prototype which fields a page shows, while its claim 13 gives V4 the fields a record captures, and its own closing claim says the ruling changes nothing else in the backlog, so it does not withdraw a ruling that decided this very step. prototype-dr2-1-source-p8-083 and prototype-dr2-1-specs-p3-060 are not overruled, because their section heading, labels and field order still stand and are built on by req-638, req-640, req-641 and req-645; only the absence of County in their field list is departed from. conflicts.about: What a journey-added address record holds: the prototype's section as the address's type, or roles only with the type derived by the INS front door.

conflicts.question: Which CDP environments must the add-address hand-off be proved in, and what counts as proof there, given the hand-off cannot run in the animals frontend's stub mode at all?
conflicts.default: Each environment gets what it can carry: the local Docker stack and the CI Docker stack the pull request runs use are proved by the tests repo's existing hand-off specs, which run only where both frontends are up; CDP dev and test, where both frontends and the address book are deployed, are proved by the same specs in the scheduled CDP run; CDP environments without both frontends and the animals frontend's stub mode are out, and the pickers there show no add control.

conflicts.about: Whether the address book's add-details step asks for a county.

conflicts.about: Which environments' saved addresses are deleted when the address book starts storing roles, beyond dev, test and a local stack.

Roles are optional on the stored document, so a record can be held with none.

Each part of the target therefore gets what the default below says until the owner answers, and req-2359 waits on it.
conflicts.question: Besides dev, test and a local stack, which environments have their addresses collection dropped when the address book starts storing roles, and what happens to an address already saved there?
conflicts.default: After the change is released, dev and test have the whole addresses collection dropped with CDP tooling and the address book restarted, and a local stack is restarted. perf-test and ext-test are dropped the same way when the change reaches them, because their addresses are test data too. conflicts.about: Whether an add reached from a notification journey shows the roles question with the hand-off's role ticked, or hides it and applies that role on its own.

A journey section starting an address book add records where to return and suggests that section's address type.

conflicts.question: On an add reached from a notification journey, is the roles question shown with the hand-off's party role already ticked, or hidden with that role applied on save?

The ticked role is kept whatever else the trader ticks, so the journey always gets an address it can select.

conflicts.about: What the addresses section, card and task row on the templates pages are called: the prototype's two names, or the one wording the owner gave on 17 November.

conflicts.outcome: The 25 November ruling wins over the 9 October afternoon claim, which it names as an error: every plants picker pages at eight and keeps the restatement of the chosen address. That is what the plants records already describe, so the plants records stand and the pickers need no ledger entry.

conflicts.about: Which high-risk plants pages are signed off, when the engine reads a maturity level from each page but the set's records do not say which page holds which level.

positions.says: A page's maturity is one of exploring, detailing, agreed or readyForLive, a page that sets none is treated as exploring, and a page at agreed or readyForLive counts as signed off.
The set's docs do not say which pages are at which maturity level, so they do not show which pages of the journey are signed off.

conflicts.outcome: Left open. An increment that changes a plants page has to know whether it is changing agreed behaviour, and the set's own records answer that for no page; the one source says both that the level decides it and that the level is not written down anywhere a reader can find it.
conflicts.question: Which high-risk plants pages are at agreed or readyForLive, so an increment that changes one knows it is changing a signed-off page?
conflicts.default: Each page's level is read from its own page identity module and nowhere else, and a page whose module names no level is treated as below agreed, so no plants change is held as a change to a signed-off page unless that page's own module says agreed or readyForLive.

conflicts.about: Whether a journey page's context is carried as the trail the service now writes in the page's address, or as the ?change=1 flag and no trail that the 9 October ruling kept

positions.says: The amend controls keep their content with no action field; exit=hub and ?change=1 stay.
No ?from=hub marker is added; only the live flow's fallback changes.
The return links are treated as blocked, waiting on the save and continue theme, and build once that work has merged.
A journey page's URL may carry a from= query holding the trail of pages the trader came through.
A journey page's address carries the places the trader came by as a from= query, newest last, with the overview, the dashboard and the Import Notification Service as its starting places.
Every journey page's address carries a trail of the places the trader has saved before it.

conflicts.outcome: Unsettled, and the two readings build different services. The 9 October ruling kept ?change=1 and added no marker, and on its plain reading the trail that the save and continue work has since merged into both frontends comes out and the review context goes back to ?change=1. The other reading is that how a service remembers where a trader came from is its own architecture, which the ruling described rather than decided, and that the 10 November ruling deferred the return links to exactly that merged work; the trail then stays and the return and Back rules are specified against it. Precedence ranks neither, because the later ruling defers to the work that built the trail while the earlier one names the flag, so the question goes to the owner. Nothing about where a saved page or a Back link goes turns on the answer: req-1615, req-1616, req-1639 and req-1917 state those destinations without naming the mechanism.
conflicts.question: Does the journey keep the trail it now writes into each page's address as the way it remembers where a trader came from, or come off it and go back to the ?change=1 flag with no trail?
conflicts.default: The trail stays, in both frontends. A page's address carries the places already saved, newest last, in the service's own names; the review context is the review page's own place on that trail instead of ?change=1; and no page of the merged save and continue work is reverted. New work specifies the return and Back rules by where the trader came from rather than by the query that records it.

conflicts.about: Where a page opened from a Change link on the review page goes when it is saved

positions.says: On look and feel the prototype wins by default over what the real services do today.
A section page returns to the review page when it continues and was reached from the review.
Save and continue on a page opened by a Change link goes on to the next journey page rather than straight back to the review.
Pressing Save and continue from a page opened by a Change link walks every later journey page in turn and ends on the review.
Saving the accompanying documents page opened on the review trail opens the consignment addresses page.

conflicts.outcome: Design Release 2.1 outranks what the real frontend does today and no DR1 judgement or real constraint covers it: a page opened from the review page returns to the review page when it is saved. Walking the rest of the journey from a Change link is set aside. repo-frontend-p3-084 is not set aside, because it also records that the review offers a 'Change document 1' link that opens the accompanying documents page, which stays true.

conflicts.about: Which environments every link, redirect and form hand-over between services has to work in, and how that is proved

positions.says: Links between services must work in CDP, in the local Docker stack and in the CI Docker stack, all three.
The ruling names CDP as a whole and no environment within it, such as dev, test or production.
The ruling does not say how working links in all three environments are to be proved, so no check or evidence is named.
The Import Notification Service's type-question URL is built from the configured base URL with any trailing slash removed.

conflicts.outcome: The ruling cannot be met as written in every part of the target: it names CDP as a whole, and the programme deploys to some CDP environments and not others, while the two Docker stacks have an end-to-end suite that can prove a link and CDP has none. Two readings build different things — one proves every link in every CDP environment, the other proves what each environment can prove and takes the rest from one shared configuration — and nothing ranks them, so the question goes to the owner with a default that says what each part gets.
conflicts.question: Which CDP environments must every link, redirect and form hand-over between services be proved to work in, and what counts as proof there?
conflicts.default: Each link, redirect and form hand-over resolves from the calling service's own configuration with no hard-coded host or port. It is proved in the local Docker stack and the continuous-integration Docker stack by the end-to-end suite walking the hand-over, and in CDP dev and test by one walk of the journey on the deployed services. CDP perf, pre-production and production take the same configuration and get no proof in this programme.

conflicts.about: What proves a plants page this programme changes, given the plants domain has end-to-end and visual specs only and no accessibility or security specs.

positions.says: Where plants has the same page or behaviour, the same increment changes plants too.
The plants domain has docker-compose scripts for end-to-end and visual only, and none for accessibility or security.
No attacking spec exists for the high-risk plants journey, so the plants backend is declared as a context with an attack job of its own that nothing drives.
Neither the per-domain script table nor the profile table says whether plants' missing accessibility and security suites are planned or deliberately out of scope.

conflicts.outcome: Nothing ranks the two readings. The owner's rule that plants takes the same change in the same increment can be read as carrying the animals proof across, which would mean writing plants an accessibility suite and a security corpus, or as carrying only the change, which leaves a changed plants page proved by the end-to-end and visual specs it has. Neither the rulings nor the tests repo's own documentation settles it, so it goes to the owner with a default.
conflicts.question: When an increment changes a plants page as well as an animals one, does plants get accessibility and security specs for that page, or is its end-to-end and visual proof enough?
conflicts.default: Animals and INS pages keep their existing accessibility and security suites. A plants page this programme changes is proved by the plants domain's end-to-end and visual specs and by the plants frontend's own in-repo checks, and no plants accessibility specs or attacking security specs are written; the full attacking run keeps failing its no-traffic gate on the plants backend context, so only per-domain attacking runs are used, and that gap goes to the report.
